---
title: "Indicator: Life satisfaction, British Columbia"
---

*Status: a published indicator from the survey family (milestone M3 in
progress). Regenerate with `uv run sohbc build life_satisfaction_bc`.*

This indicator widens the project beyond mortality. It is fetched from a
catalogued Statistics Canada table, tidied by the same pipeline as the
[mortality](indicator-mortality-rates-bc.qmd) and [life
expectancy](indicator-life-expectancy-bc.qmd) indicators, and published as
a versioned dataset plus the views below. The whole survey family is
described on the [CCHS indicator page](indicator-wellbeing-cchs-bc.qmd).

## Provenance

| Field | Value |
|-------|-------|
| **Domain** | [Subjective wellbeing](../reference/measurement-framework.qmd) |
| **Definition** | Percent of British Columbians aged 18 and over who report being satisfied or very satisfied with life, annual 2015–2025 [@statcan_health_indicators] |
| **Source** | Statistics Canada, table 13-10-0905-01, *Health indicator statistics, annual estimates* (Canadian Community Health Survey) [@statcan_health_indicators] |
| **Access** | Statistics Canada Web Data Service (automated full-table download) |
| **Form** | indicator table (published survey summary statistics) |
| **Geography** | British Columbia (no sub-provincial rows in this table) |
| **Coverage** | 2015–2025 (annual); observation window shown on each figure |
| **Frequency / refresh** | annual |
| **Licence** | Statistics Canada Open Licence |
| **Proxy note** | A self-reported proxy in the wellbeing domain, not the state of health itself ([why](../explanation/definition-of-health.qmd#proxies-are-not-the-state-of-health)) |

## Trend

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
rows = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_satisfaction_bc.csv").csv({typed: true})
bySex = rows.filter(d => d.sex !== "Both sexes")
headline = rows.filter(d => d.sex === "Both sexes")
trend = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_satisfaction_bc_trend.json").json()
bySexTrend = await FileAttachment("../data/published/life_satisfaction_bc_by_sex_trend.json").json()
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
Plot.plot({
  title: "Life satisfaction (satisfied or very satisfied), British Columbia (% of adults)",
  x: {label: "Year", tickFormat: "d"},
  y: {grid: true, label: "% of adults aged 18+", domain: [70, 100]},
  color: {legend: true},
  marks: [
    Plot.rectX([{x1: 2020, x2: 2025}], {x1: "x1", x2: "x2", fill: "grey", fillOpacity: 0.12}),
    Plot.ruleX(bySexTrend.levels["Both sexes"].change_points, {stroke: "red", strokeDasharray: "4,4"}),
    Plot.lineY(bySex, {x: "ref_date", y: "value", stroke: "sex", tip: true}),
    Plot.dot(bySex, {x: "ref_date", y: "value", stroke: "sex", tip: true}),
    Plot.lineY(headline, {x: "ref_date", y: "value", stroke: "black", strokeWidth: 2.5, tip: true}),
    Plot.dot(headline, {x: "ref_date", y: "value", stroke: "black", tip: true})
  ]
})
```

The black line is both sexes, the coloured lines are the source's sex
categories. The grey band marks the COVID-19 period (2020–2025); the red
dashed line is the regime break dated by the pipeline.

## Trajectory and regimes

Trend summaries, recomputed on every build
(`data/published/life_satisfaction_bc_trend.json`,
`data/published/life_satisfaction_bc_by_sex_trend.json`):

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
md`Over ${trend.start}–${trend.end} life satisfaction (both sexes)
changed by **${trend.overall.slope_per_decade.toFixed(2)}** percentage
points per decade, and the series is **${trend.stationarity.verdict}**. It
carries a downward rank trend (Kendall's tau =
${trend.trend_test.tau.toFixed(2)}, p =
${trend.trend_test.p_value.toFixed(3)}) and a departure from a single
straight line (residual-permutation test, p =
${trend.break_test.p_value.toFixed(3)}). The BIC-selected regimes break at
${trend.change_points.join(", ")}: **${trend.segments[0].slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}** pp/decade
before, **${trend.segments[1].slope_per_decade.toFixed(1)}** pp/decade
from ${trend.segments[1].start}.`
```

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
sexRows = ["Both sexes", "Males", "Females"].map(sex => ({
  sex,
  ...bySexTrend.levels[sex]
})).map(d => ({
  sex: d.sex,
  slope_per_decade: d.overall.slope_per_decade,
  verdict: d.stationarity.verdict,
  change_points: d.change_points.join(", ") || "—",
  change_point: d.change_point ?? "—"
}))
Inputs.table(sexRows, {
  columns: ["sex", "slope_per_decade", "verdict", "change_points", "change_point"],
  header: {sex: "sex", slope_per_decade: "slope/decade (pp)", verdict: "stationarity", change_points: "regime breaks", change_point: "largest break"}
})
```

**Method.** Regimes are dated by a piecewise-linear segmentation, solved
exactly by dynamic programming, with the number of breaks chosen by BIC;
whether the series departs from one straight line is tested by residual
permutation [@truong2020selective], and the trend by Kendall's tau. Each
series is therefore labelled stationary or not over its observed window,
as milestone M3 requires. The full test output, including every candidate
segmentation, is in the trend JSON. The permutation test assumes
exchangeable residuals — autocorrelation is not modelled — so it is a
test of departure from a linear trend, not a full time-series model.

## Caveats

- **Survey estimate.** Life satisfaction is self-reported on a national
  survey; it carries sampling error and a coefficient-of-variation release
  policy, so individual cells may be suppressed or flagged. The plotted
  series are the published point estimates.
- **Measurement, not only change.** The CCHS collection frame changed over
  the series and 2020–2021 collection was disrupted by the pandemic
  [@statcan_health_indicators]. Part of any break may be a change in *how*
  the series was measured, not only in how people answered. The pipeline
  dates the break; it does not attribute it.
- **Break detection, not explanation.** The regimes are dated by a formal
  test (above); the test says a break beyond a single straight line
  exists, not what caused it.
- **Sex categories are the source's.** The table publishes both sexes,
  males, and females; the pipeline reports these as given.
- **No sub-provincial rows.** The source table is provincial only;
  health-authority and regional survey series are separate products.
- **Revisions.** Statistics Canada may revise survey estimates; the
  published files are regenerated from the source on each build.

## Reproduce

```bash
uv run sohbc fetch statcan_health_indicators
uv run sohbc build life_satisfaction_bc
```

The tidy dataset is published at
`data/published/life_satisfaction_bc.csv` (by sex). The headline trend test
is at `data/published/life_satisfaction_bc_trend.json` and the per-sex
tests at `data/published/life_satisfaction_bc_by_sex_trend.json`.
